42859213.label: Background
42859213.text: Nuclear β-catenin accumulation reflects activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but noninvasive preoperative prediction of this immunohistochemical phenotype remains incompletely established.

42859213.label: Purpose
42859213.text: To develop and externally validate CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) models for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC.

42859213.label: Materials and methods
42859213.text: This multicenter retrospective study included 1029 patients with histopathologically confirmed HCC. Patients from two participating institutions formed the development cohort and were split into training (n=620; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 293) and internal validation (n=267; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 126) sets. Patients from an independent third institution formed the external validation cohort (n=142; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 43). Whole-tumor portal venous phase CT radiomics features and topology-based ITH features were extracted from the audited image-mask cohort. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using AUC, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, calibration summaries, Brier scores, and decision curve analysis.

42859213.label: Results
42859213.text: In external validation, AUCs were 0.677 for the clinical model, 0.862 for the radiomics model, 0.857 for the ITH model, 0.831 for the core ITH model, 0.863 for the radiomics-ITH model, and 0.886 for the stacking model. Compared with radiomics alone, stacking showed a numerical ΔAUC of 0.024 (95% CI, -0.010 to 0.060; P=0.180).

42859213.label: Conclusion
42859213.text: CT radiomics and topology-based ITH features showed external predictive value for nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. The stacking model had the highest external AUC, but its improvement over radiomics alone was not statistically significant. If prospectively validated, these CT-based approaches could complement tissue assessment for pretreatment biological stratification.

42875613.label: Objectives
42875613.text: To develop and evaluate a method to predict glomerular filtration rate (GFR) from clinical renal CT.

42875613.label: Materials and methods
42875613.text: Medical records of adult living kidney donors operated between 2013 and 2022 and patients considered for neoadjuvant cisplatin prior to cystectomy between 2019 and 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Inclusion criteria were (1) renal CT obtained at 100 or 120 kVp before and 5-15 min after contrast administration, and (2) iohexol clearance test within 2 months of imaging. The iohexol clearance test was performed on the same day as the cystatin C and creatinine measurements. Estimated GFR values included cystatin C-based eGFR (eGFRcystatin C), creatinine-based eGFR using the Cockcroft-Gault formula (eGFRCockcroft-Gault), and eGFR using the Revised Lund-Malmö formula (eGFRLMR18), which is based on both creatinine and cystatin C. Manual and automatic segmentations of the renal pelvis and bladder were performed in both the excretory and unenhanced phases.

42875613.label: Results
42875613.text: In total, 139 patients were included in the analysis (mean age 52 ± 13 years; 60% women). Multivariate linear regression analysis combining the segmentation-derived variable with body surface area and age gave an adjusted R-square of 0.77 to mGFRiohexol (p < 0.001). GFRCT had the strongest relationship to mGFRiohexol with a mean absolute error of 12.8 mL/min, compared with 15.6 mL/min for eGFRCockcroft-Gault, 14.2 mL/min for eGFRcystatin C, and 13.0 mL/min for eGFRLMR18. Manual and automatic segmentations had similar performance. Patients evaluated for cisplatin treatment had greater variation in CT-estimated split renal function than donors.

42875613.label: Conclusion
42875613.text: Renal function can be estimated with high precision from clinical renal CT.

42875613.label: Key points
42875613.text: Question Accurate GFR assessment is critical, but current methods are either labor-intensive or imprecise. Can renal CT imaging provide a reliable alternative? Findings CT-derived eGFR showed the strongest correlation with iohexol clearance (R² = 0.77), with lower error compared to creatinine- and cystatin C-based estimates. Critical relevance statement Routine CT imaging can provide precise estimates of kidney function, supporting donor evaluations, chemotherapy dosing, and critical care decisions when accurate renal function is essential.

42955613.text: To synthesise evidence on the diagnostic performance, safety, feasibility and clinical impact of ultra-low-field portable magnetic resonance imaging (pMRI) in adult neurocritical care and intensive care unit (ICU) populations. PubMed, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 6 February 2026 and supplemented by grey literature and citation searching. We included original English-language studies of adult ICU, neurocritical care or emergency department patients undergoing pMRI at ≤ 0.1 T. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias in diagnostic comparisons was assessed with an adapted QUADAS-2 framework, and feasibility and safety outcomes were appraised narratively. Because of heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. Eleven studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included, comprising 694 patient participants and 715 patient examinations, plus 40 healthy controls. Cohorts overlapped substantially: six studies came wholly and one partly from a single institution, and one ECMO study was a subset of another. The number of unique patients is therefore estimated at 281 to 677. In the multicentre ECMO study, adverse events occurred in 3 of 50 patients (6%). One was serious: an intra-aortic balloon pump malfunction attributed to electrocardiographic artefact. No adverse events were reported in the other seven independent cohorts that reported safety outcomes, and two studies did not report safety outcomes. For ischaemic stroke, pMRI detected infarction in 45 of 50 patients (90%). By sequence, sensitivity was 100% for FLAIR, 98% for T2-weighted imaging and 86% for diffusion-weighted imaging. Visual DWI-FLAIR mismatch identified patients scanned within 4.5 h with 60% sensitivity, 82% specificity and a 93% negative predictive value. Sensitivity for intracerebral haemorrhage was 80.4% (specificity 96.6%) on initial blinded evaluation. It was 92.1% (specificity 99.3%) in a later cohort in which raters had clinical context and images used deep-learning reconstruction, with lower sensitivity for infratentorial haemorrhage (75.0%). Only one subdural haemorrhage and no extradural haemorrhages were reported. Midline-shift detection showed 93% sensitivity, 96% specificity and a kappa of 0.87. pMRI detected hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury in 12 of 12 affected post-cardiac-arrest patients. In ECMO patients, pMRI detected 8 of 8 ischaemic events, compared with 4 of 8 on head CT, but only 1 of 2 haemorrhages. Up to 28% of examinations were nondiagnostic, mainly because of motion. Ultra-low-field pMRI is a feasible bedside neuroimaging adjunct with a low but non-zero adverse-event rate. It is of particular value for ischaemic injury, midline shift and serial monitoring. Lower and variable sensitivity for haemorrhage, the nonspecificity of FLAIR hyperintensity, overlapping single-institution cohorts and small samples mean that larger multicentre validation studies are needed.

42988563.text: Radiopharmaceutical therapy with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) radioligands has emerged as a promising treatment modality for metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer). Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling has been applied in clinical studies of PSMA radioligands. However, clinical models are necessarily simplified because of sparse patient data, which may mask important pharmacokinetic processes. The aim of this study was to perform PBPK modeling on comprehensive preclinical data and identify previously neglected dynamics of PSMA radioligands with translation relevance. Methods: Biodistribution and albumin-binding affinity data were previously obtained for the 2 PSMA radioligands [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 and [177Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T and the 3 albumin-binding PSMA radioligands [177Lu]Lu-SibuDAB, [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-ALB-53, and [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-ALB-56. A baseline, preclinical PBPK model was built using a widely studied radioligand PBPK model structure. Three types of modifications to the baseline model were developed: nonspecific retention in PSMA-negative tissues and kidneys, change from an irreversible to a reversible albumin-binding model, and albumin-bound fraction implementation. Models with modification combinations were built, and regressions were performed against the biodistribution data. The modifications were evaluated on the regression performances, and simulations of the fitted models were compared with clinically established baseline regressions through time-integrated activity (TIA) ratios. Results: For all radioligands, incorporating nonspecific retention markedly improved the corrected Akaike information criterion (AIC). The reversible albumin-binding model showed improved AIC for all albumin-binding radioligands. The implementation of albumin-bound fractions degraded the AIC but showed minor impact on fits. With nonspecific retention, substantial increases in TIAs were observed for PSMA-negative organs, particularly for the dose-limited organ red marrow where TIA ratios reached 3.0, 1.5, and 1.6 for [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617, [177Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T, and [177Lu]Lu-SibuDAB, respectively. TIAs for PSMA-positive tissues and kidneys remained relatively stable. Conclusion: This preclinical study demonstrated that disregarding nonspecific retention led to marked underestimation of doses to PSMA-negative tissues such as in the radiosensitive red marrow. The models with reversible albumin-binding further improved the regressions for the albumin-binding radioligands but had limited impact on TIA estimates. By integrating these mechanisms, preclinical PBPK models provide novel insights into radioligand kinetics and can inform the refinement of clinical PBPK models toward safer and more individualized PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy.

42998163.label: Objectives
42998163.text: Chemotherapy-associated steatohepatitis (CASH) increases the risk of postoperative liver failure and mortality in patients undergoing liver surgery. However, non-invasive diagnosis remains an unmet need. Radiomics has potential for characterizing liver parenchyma. This study evaluated the performance of a virtual liver biopsy for CASH prediction, comparing it with whole-liver radiomic analysis.

42998163.label: Materials and methods
42998163.text: Two retrospective series of patients undergoing hepatectomy for colorectal liver metastases were analyzed: the public "Colorectal-Liver-Metastases" dataset (training and internal validation) and a monocenter series from Humanitas Research Hospital (external validation). Inclusion criteria were preoperative chemotherapy (≥ 2 months) and post-chemotherapy CT (thickness ≤ 5 mm). IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted from whole-liver parenchyma and from a virtual biopsy (manually segmented 2-mL cylinder of non-tumoral liver parenchyma). Estimated liver volume (eLV) was computed using three orthogonal diameters. Four XGBoost models were developed (70/30 split, 5-fold cross-validation): clinical; clinical + VB-radiomics (ViB); clinical + VB-radiomics + eLV (ViBE+); clinical + whole-liver radiomics (WholeLiver).

42998163.label: Results
42998163.text: One hundred eighty patients were included: 105 internal (63 males, mean age 58.9 years, 38% CASH+) and 75 external (44 males, mean age 62.4 years, 19% CASH+). WholeLiver and ViBE+ models achieved excellent and comparable performance in internal validation (WholeLiver: AUC = 0.857 (95% BS-CI: 0.676-0.954), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903); ViBE + : AUC = 0.831 (95% BS-CI: 0.549-0.956), accuracy = 0.839 (95% BS-CI: 0.710-0.935); p = 0.814), outperforming ViB model (AUC = 0.724 (95% BS-CI: 0.483-0.896), accuracy = 0.774 (95% BS-CI: 0.613-0.903)). SHAP analysis confirmed liver volume metrics as key predictors. In external validation, the ViBE+ model achieved AUC = 0.745 (95% BS-CI: 0.604-0.886) and accuracy = 0.680 (95% BS-CI: 0.562-0.783).

42998163.label: Conclusion
42998163.text: Virtual biopsy provides a reproducible, non-invasive radiomic sampling strategy for CASH prediction. Combined with liver volume metrics, it achieves performance comparable to whole-liver analysis, supporting its potential clinical application.

42998163.label: Key points
42998163.text: Question Despite its association with postoperative morbidity, the non-invasive preoperative assessment of CASH remains challenging in patients undergoing liver surgery. Findings Radiomic analysis based on a virtual liver biopsy, combined with volumetric measurements, showed excellent performance in predicting CASH, comparable to whole-liver analysis, with liver volume emerging as a key predictor. Critical Relevance Statement A standardized virtual biopsy-based radiomic analysis represents a promising non-invasive approach for evaluating liver parenchymal injury, as demonstrated in preoperative assessment of CASH and identification of high-risk surgical patients.

43019563.text: A 1-year-old girl with clinical and imaging features suggestive of neuroblastoma was enrolled in our prospective diagnostic trial. She underwent 18F-MFBG PET/CT for tumor characterization. On tomographic images, focal 18F-MFBG uptake, manifesting as an elongated linear pattern, was observed along the left aspect of the spinal canal spanning vertebral levels L2-L5. Contrast-enhanced MRI revealed no structural correlate. The source of this linear uptake remains uncertain. It may represent benign vascular activity, possibly involving the vertebral venous plexus, although this remains unconfirmed. Recognition of this potential pitfall is important to avoid misinterpretation as metastasis.

43097113.label: Purpose
43097113.text: To evaluate the role of 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and the histopathology analysis in patients with suspected insulinoma.

43097113.label: Methods
43097113.text: 100 patients with suspected insulinoma were enrolled. Diagnostic performance, semi-quantitative parameter values, and immunoreactivity score (IRS) were compared. Correlation of GLP-1R and SSTR2 IRS was analyzed with semi-quantitative parameters, maximum tumor diameter, and Ki-67 index.

43097113.label: Results
43097113.text: 51 patients and 11 patients were confirmed as insulinoma with histopathology and consensus of the multidisciplinary team (MDT), respectively. The combination of 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT achieved superior diagnostic performance, reducing false-negative results compared to single-tracer PET/CT. The dual-tracer PET/CT demonstrated higher sensitivity, accuracy, and negative predictive value (NPV) than 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 (NPV, p < 0.05) and 68Ga-DOTATATE (all p < 0.001). In G1 lesions, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT showed significantly higher SUVmax (49.55 ± 37.69 vs. 22.46 ± 14.38, p = 0.035) and TBR (12.38 ± 6.55 vs. 6.71 ± 4.59, p = 0.029) than 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT. These results were in accordance with elevated SSTR2 IRS compared with GLP-1R IRS (8.60 ± 1.92 vs. 6.01 ± 1.87, p = 0.002). In G2 lesions, SUVmax, TBR, and GLP-1R IRS were slightly higher on 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT (p > 0.05). SSTR2 IRS was positively associated with maximum tumor diameter (r = 0.358, p = 0.025) and negatively associated with the Ki-67 index (r = -0.547, p < 0.001). SUVmax and TBR of 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT showed positive correlations with their corresponding IRS (all p < 0.01).

43097113.label: Conclusion
43097113.text: 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT is recommended as the first-line functional imaging modality for patients with suspected insulinoma. When 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT shows negative results, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT serves a complementary role. These were in accordance with the different expression of GLP-1R and SSTR2 between G1 and G2 insulinomas.

43102613.label: Background
43102613.text: We developed and validated a portal venous phase CT-based model that combines topological intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH), radiomics, and clinicoradiological features for preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We also examined whether three-dimensional (3D) ITH was associated with transcriptomic and immune-related features in an exploratory radiogenomic cohort.

43102613.label: Methods
43102613.text: This multicenter retrospective study included 821 surgically confirmed HCC patients in training (n = 489), internal validation (n = 211), and external validation (n = 121) cohorts. Manually segmented tumors were used to develop clinical, ITH, radiomics, and stacking ensemble models. Time to recurrence (TTR) and SHAP-based model interpretation were analyzed; mortality data were not collected, and death was therefore not incorporated into this recurrence endpoint. A separate supplementary, hypothesis-generating analysis of 42 TCGA-LIHC cases explored transcriptomic correlates of 3D ITH; differential-expression and gene-set analyses used Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery rate (FDR) correction.

43102613.label: Results
43102613.text: The ensemble achieved AUCs of 0.805 (95% CI, 0.760-0.847), 0.851 (95% CI, 0.796-0.902), and 0.757 (95% CI, 0.648-0.855) in the training out-of-fold, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. The ITH model showed comparable and numerically slightly higher AUCs than the radiomics model, but paired DeLong tests did not show statistically significant differences. SHAP analysis ranked the 3D ITH score as the leading contributor within the ensemble, and both the 3D ITH score and ensemble risk score were associated with TTR. The supplementary TCGA-LIHC analysis generated exploratory associations between 3D ITH and survival and pathway-level transcriptomic patterns.

43102613.label: Conclusions
43102613.text: Portal venous CT-derived topological ITH provided interpretable information for preoperative MVI prediction and recurrence-risk assessment in HCC. The supplementary radiogenomic observations are hypothesis-generating.

43104163.label: Purpose
43104163.text: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) is an established therapeutic option for advanced somatostatin-receptor-expressing neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) patients. However, reproducible PET-derived biomarkers to stratify patients before treatment remain incompletely defined. This study evaluated whether pre-PRRT PET-derived parameters were associated with outcome.

43104163.label: Methods
43104163.text: This single-center retrospective observational study included NET patients studied with baseline [68Ga]Ga-DOTANOC PET/CT before [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE PRRT. Candidate PET-variables included whole-body and site-specific MITV (molecular imaging tumour volume), MITV*SUVmean, MITV-to-SUVmean ratios. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates, univariable Cox-regression, LASSO-Cox regression for variable selection, and final multivariable Cox models.

43104163.label: Results
43104163.text: Forty-one patients were included; at a median follow-up of 42.6 months (95%CI, 39.9-62.1), 25 PFS events and 10 deaths occurred. Median-PFS was 35.6 months (95% CI, 26.2 months to not reached), whereas median-OS was not reached. In the final multivariable PFS model, TotalMITV-to-SUVmean ratio remained independently associated with PFS (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.003-1.085; p = 0.032), whereas NodesMITV did not reach statistical significance. In the multivariable OS model, TotalMITV-to-SUVmean ratio (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 1.01-1.12; p = 0.024) and Ki67 (HR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.05-1.37; p = 0.007) were associated with OS, whereas surgery of the primary tumour was not. Patients with a TotalMITV-to-SUVmean ratio above the cohort median had shorter median-PFS (26.2 vs. 38.1 months).

43104163.label: Conclusion
43104163.text: Pre-PRRT [68Ga]Ga-DOTANOC TotalMITV-to-SUVmean ratio was independently associated with PFS and showed a supportive association with OS. This composite parameter, capturing the relationship between SSTR-PET-defined tumour burden and mean tracer uptake intensity, warrants external validation.
